items.title: you need to self-host Github RIGHT NOW!!
items.summary:
Get your own home lab in the cloud with a Hostinger VPS, and use code NETWORKCHUCK for an extra discount: https://ntck.co/hostinger-gitea

When GitHub goes down, your work goes down with it, and Microsoft holds your code. So I self-host my own GitHub with Gitea, a free, open source Git server that looks and works a lot like GitHub, and I've been running it for six months. In this video I set it up from scratch on a Hostinger VPS, push my Git Good repo from the Git video into it, then give my AI agent its own account and connect Claude Code through the official Gitea MCP server so it can work issues and open pull requests on a server I own. Then I do the same thing with a local AI model running on my own computer, mirror everything to GitHub so it can still be public, and lock the server down. In this video you'll learn how to install Gitea with Docker Compose, get free HTTPS from Let's Encrypt, the two setup page settings you must change, how to make Gitea your Git remote, how to give
